Aadhaar-linked bank accounts, Direct Benefit Transfer, e-KYC and digital verification strengthen transparency and reduce intermediaries. The scheme’s continuation until 2030-31, backed by a ₹ 3.15 lakh crore financial outlay, reinforces sustained support for farmer income security.
PM-KISAN: Strengthening Income Security for Farmers
The government has released the 24 th instalment of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) on 30 October 2026, at Banaskantha, Gujarat . More than 9.34 crore eligible farmers received around ₹ 18,690 crore in direct financial assistance. The funds were transferred through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system , ensuring transparency and eliminating intermediaries. The scheme is widely regarded as a significant initiative towards ensuring ‘ Annadata Samman’ .
Recently, in July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved continuation of the PM-KISAN Scheme from 2026-27 to 2030-31. A total financial outlay of ₹ 3.15 lakh crore has been approved for the scheme during this period. The approval reiterates the government’s commitment that the prosperity of farmers forms the foundation of the nation’s prosperity.
Direct Income Support to Small and Marginal Farmers under PM-KISAN
PM-KISAN is a centrally sponsored scheme launched on February 24, 2019. The scheme seeks to provide assured income support to landholding farmer families nationwide with cultivable land. Under the scheme, each eligible farmer family receives annual financial assistance of ₹6,000 . This is disbursed in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 into their Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts .
The assistance provided under PM-KISAN has enabled farmers to make timely investments in seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, agricultural machinery and other agricultural requirements. This has enhanced farmers’ productive capacity , reduced their dependence on informal credit and strengthened the financial stability of rural households .
So far, more than ₹ 4.64 lakh crore has been disbursed to eligible farmer families across the country through 24 instalments. The scheme benefits are provided to farmers after their land records are seeded on the PM-KISAN portal. They also must link their bank accounts to Aadhaar and complete e-KYC verification . Reflecting the government’s continued commitment to strengthening farmers’ income security, the Union Budget 2026-27 has allocated ₹ 60,000 crore for the PM-KISAN scheme.

articles.full_content:
ICAR–NBAIR, Bengaluru organized the live webcast of the ‘Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)’ programme addressed by the Hon’ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi for the benefit of farmers particularly Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) on October 30, 2026, at ICAR-NBAIR, Yelahanka campus. The event was graced by Dr. Y.N. Shivalingaiah Hon’ble Dean (Agri.), University of Agricultural Sciences, GKVK, Bengaluru, as the Chief Guest, in the presence of Dr. T. Venkatesan, Director, ICAR–NBAIR.
In his opening remarks Dr. T. Venkatesan briefed the dignitaries and participants about the various activities of ICAR-NBAIR and the role of the institute in supporting farmers by the development of various biological control technologies for the successful pest management. He advocated the farmers for the adoption of eco-friendly methods to restore the soil health and created awareness about the need for sustainable agriculture.
Chief Guest Dr. Y.N. Shivalingaiah highlighted the importance of PM-KISAN flagship programme, wherein Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi released the 24 th instalment of ₹18,690.32 crore Samman Rashi directly to the bank accounts of more than 9.34 crore eligible farmers via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) from Banaskantha, Gujarat.
In his address, he stated that the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is keen to improve the prosperity of farmers in our country. He emphasised the importance of crop rotation, integrated nutrient and pest management. He advised farmers to use biocontrol agents and bio-rational technologies for the successful management of pest and disease control for sustainable agriculture.
The virtual event marking the release of the 24 th instalment of the PM-KISAN Scheme by the Prime Minister was witnessed by 150 people including 113 farmers, besides students and researchers. As part of the programme, biocontrol inputs were distributed to farmers from Kolar District of Karnataka under the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC).

ICAR-National Research Centre for Orchids, Pakyong joins the Nation in celebrating PM-KISAN Utsav Diwas
The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi today released the 24th instalment of Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) from Banaskantha, Gujarat, transferring more than Rs. 18,690 crore directly to the bank accounts of over 9.34 crore farmers across the country through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). On the occasion, the Prime Minister also dedicated to the nation 521 units developed under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund and inaugurated 12 Horticulture Clusters.
Joining the nationwide celebration, ICAR-National Research Centre for Orchids (NRCO), Pakyong organized “PM-KISAN Utsav” with organic farmers of Pakyong District.
A total of 85 farmers/beneficiaries from Ganchung, Damlakha, Taza, Pachak, Parkha, Kabuthang, Taksang, Mamjey, Yakten, Pakyong, Chalamthung, Pachey, Kartok and Namcheybong villages of Pakyong District participated in the programme and witnessed the live telecast of the Prime Minister’s address.
The PM-KISAN scheme, a Central Sector Scheme launched on 24th February 2019, aims to provide financial support to all landholding farmer families with cultivable land. Under the scheme, eligible farmers receive Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000 each. Farmers can self-register through the PM-Kisan portal, mobile application and Common Service Centres, with land records digitally verified and the amount transferred directly to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts through DBT, ensuring transparency and timely delivery.
As one of the world’s largest DBT programmes, PM-KISAN has significantly impacted farmers by providing direct financial support. Notably, around 25% of the total benefits go to women beneficiaries. Women farmers have received more than Rs. 1.06 lakh crore under PM-KISAN till the 23rd instalment, with nearly one out of every four beneficiaries being a woman farmer, reflecting the Government’s commitment to empowering women farmers and enhancing their economic security.
The programme at ICAR-NRCO, Pakyong was organized under the leadership of Dr. S.P. Das, Director, and coordinated by Dr. L.C. De, Nodal Officer, with support from Scientists Dr. N.S. Kalaivanan, Dr. Nikhila V.A. and Dr. T. Rihne, along with Administrative, Financial, Technical, Supporting staff, Young Professionals and Contractual staff.
The programme evoked a positive response from the farmers and beneficiaries of Pakyong District.

Union Minister Bandi Sanjay Kumar Calls for Innovative Research to Enhance Farm Productivity
Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar urged agricultural researchers to develop new crop varieties through innovative ideas, improved practices and modern technology to help farmers achieve higher yields with lower investments, while conserving the environment and protecting human health. The Minister attended the Farmers’ Day celebrations as the Chief Guest at the ICAR–Indian Institute of Rice Research (ICAR–IIRR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, which also featured PM-KISAN Utsav Diwas marking the release of the 24th instalment of the PM-KISAN scheme. Addressing the gathering, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar highlighted the pivotal role of farmers in realising the Prime Minister’s vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. He described ICAR as an important institution for Telangana, recognising its significant contributions to agricultural research. He noted that research institutions like ICAR have been developing new crop varieties to help farmers cultivate crops more effectively and minimise losses.
Expressing concern over the challenges and stress faced by farmers across the country, the Minister emphasised the need for continued research and innovation to address their concerns. Highlighting the role of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme in providing financial assistance to farmers, he stressed the importance of ensuring that all eligible beneficiaries receive the benefits of government welfare schemes. On the occasion, the Minister encouraged farmers to follow the guidance and recommendations of ICAR–IIRR scientists and researchers. He emphasised that adopting scientific advice and improved agricultural practices would help farmers enhance productivity and increase their yields.
In his opening remarks, Dr. M. Srinivas Prasad, Director, ICAR–IIRR, highlighted the research initiatives undertaken by the Institute in the field of agriculture to help farmers enhance agricultural productivity, improve crop health and increase their income. This was followed by an interactive session between farmers and scientists, during which ICAR–IIRR scientists showcased their latest innovations, including newly developed rice varieties, and briefed farmers on the appropriate use of pesticides. The scientists also addressed various queries raised by the farmers and provided necessary clarifications. Smt. M. Jayasree, NGO representative of Prakriti Environment Society (PES), Dr. M. Srinivas Prasad, Director, ICAR–IIRR, other dignitaries from ICAR–IIRR and around 200 farmers participated in the event.

articles.full_content:
The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Coimbatore Branch Office, organised an awareness meet for the MSME sector on coir products on 29 October 2026 at the Pollachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry, Pollachi.
The programme aimed to create awareness among coir manufacturers and other stakeholders about Indian Standards, Quality Control Orders (QCOs), and BIS certification and licensing procedures.
The programme commenced with a welcome address by Shri Rino John S, Scientist-E/Director, Bureau of Indian Standards, Coimbatore. He highlighted the importance of quality standards in promoting the manufacture of quality products and strengthening the competitiveness of MSMEs.
The programme featured addresses by guest speakers, including Shri Tariq M. Syed, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) In-charge, Tamil Nadu Coir Business Development Corporation (TANCOIR), Coimbatore; Shri Poochamy, President, Federation of Tamil Nadu State Coir Associations, Coimbatore; and Shri Gowthaman, President, Inter Continental Coir Association (ICCA). The speakers emphasised the importance of quality improvement, standardisation, and the adoption of Indian Standards in the coir sector. Their participation provided an opportunity to discuss industry requirements and strengthen cooperation among BIS, coir manufacturers, and industry associations.
Shri Rino John S, Scientist-E/Director, delivered a presentation on the activities and functions of BIS, providing an overview of its role in standardisation. He also made a technical presentation on Indian Standards and the BIS certification process for manufacturers.
In the afternoon session, a Manak Manthan technical discussion was conducted on Coir-Based Green Roof Module — Specification (IS 19727:2026) and Coir Scrub Pad — Specification (IS 19942:2026). Shri Himanshu Shukla, Member Secretary, Scientist ‘C’/Deputy Director (Textiles), BIS, explained the respective standards and facilitated discussions with industry representatives. The discussions focused on understanding the practical challenges faced by manufacturers in implementing the requirements of these standards. Industry feedback and challenges were documented for further consideration, providing a platform for interaction between BIS and stakeholders in the coir sector.
The awareness meet witnessed the participation of around 60 representatives from MSMEs in the coir sector. The programme encouraged the adoption of Indian Standards to improve product quality, promote consumer protection, and enhance the competitiveness of the industry.

Addressing sessions on the first two days of the event, Shri Naik said India’s installed electricity capacity stood at 558.9 GW as of 30 September 2026, of which about 308 GW, or 55 per cent, came from non-fossil sources. Emerging Pillar of India’s Clean Energy Transition
Green hydrogen is emerging as a pillar of India’s clean energy transition. It is produced by splitting water using renewable electricity. It can help reduce emissions in sectors such as fertiliser production, petroleum refining, iron and steel manufacturing, heavy-duty road transport and shipping . The National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) supports domestic manufacturing, production, assured demand and credible certification. From green ammonia auctions to India’s first hydrogen train, early projects point to a promising path.
Why Green Hydrogen
Hydrogen is an energy carrier that stores energy and delivers it for varied uses. In a fuel cell, it reacts with oxygen to produce electricity, leaving only water and heat as by-products, and no polluting compounds or greenhouse gases. Although pure hydrogen is not found in large quantities in nature, it can be extracted from compounds such as water or natural gas. Its environmental impact therefore depends on how it is made. Conventional methods rely on fossil fuels and release carbon emissions.
Production using renewable electricity from solar and wind power can cut this footprint substantially. Hydrogen made by splitting water using renewable power is called green hydrogen . Unlike fossil-based routes, this process emits far less carbon. India’s abundant solar and wind resources make domestic production feasible. This diversifies the country’s energy sources and strengthens energy security. It also supports India’s goal of net-zero emissions by 2070.
Green hydrogen matters most in sectors where cutting emissions is difficult. Reasons include high-temperature heat needs, chemical processes and few alternatives to fossil fuels. These hard-to-abate sectors include fertiliser, petroleum refining, iron and steel, heavy-duty road transport and shipping. Fertiliser and refining plants already use hydrogen, so green hydrogen can replace the fossil-based supply. It can also support lower-emission steelmaking, selected transport uses and energy storage. It is especially useful where direct electrification is difficult or less practical.
For India, wider adoption could reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels. It would also lessen exposure to global fuel price swings. The sector could open opportunities in manufacturing, draw investment, create jobs and expand exports. Building capabilities across the value chain would strengthen domestic supply chains and spur industrial innovation. Green hydrogen can thus support self-reliance, sustainable industrial growth and a low-carbon future.

Ministry of Textiles is set to reopen the application portal for the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles for accepting new applications under Round 4 of the Scheme from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026 to promote the manufacturing of Man-Made Fibre (MMF) Apparel, MMF Fabrics and Technical Textiles, enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, attract investment, generate employment and strengthen India's position in global textile value chains.
To facilitate wider participation under the Scheme, the following key modifications have also been made in the Scheme:
1. Reduction in Minimum Turnover Criterion: The minimum turnover requirement has been reduced from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore under Part 2 category of the scheme, enabling greater participation by MSMEs and mid-sized manufacturing units.
2. Extension of Scheme Tenure: The scheme tenure has been extended up to Financial Year 2033–34 exclusively for applicants approved under Round 4. The extended tenure is intended to provide these applicants with a longer investment and operational horizon for establishing and scaling up their manufacturing capacities.
3. Migration of Existing Participant Companies of the Scheme to Round 4 : All existing participant companies of Round 1, 2 & 3, in any part of the Scheme, that have not claimed or received any incentive so far, are also eligible to migrate under Round 4, subject to withdrawal of their existing applications under Round 1, 2 and 3, as applicable.
The online application portal https://pli.texmin.gov.in will remain open from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026 . Eligible companies are encouraged to submit their applications within the stipulated period in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines.
